Eden (People Ops): following up from today's all-hands Q&A  capturing the top asks on offer commitments, transfer timing, and appeals. i'll keep this short and sticky. :pushpin:
Vik (Eng Manager): thanks! manager question: when we say "promotion at 6 months" in an offer, is that a guaranteed pay bump?
Eden (People Ops): short answer: it's a documented commitment to review, not an automatic salary change. managers should record an "Onboarding Promotion Plan" in Offer Notes and submit a promotion packet at the agreed checkpoint. final approval depends on calibration + budget.
Ari (IC): can you paste a one-liner recruiters can copy into offers so wording is consistent?
Eden (People Ops): paste verbatim: "Onboarding Promotion Plan: target review at 6 months; measurable success criteria attached; promotion subject to calibration and budget approval."
Sofia (Recruiting): noted  we'll update the offer playbook and use that exact line to reduce negotiation back-and-forth.
finance-bot: FYI: salary changes are effective on the first payroll after HR approval. Retro-pay requires finance sign-off.
Vik (Eng Manager): transfer edge-case: someone moves teams mid-cycle with materially different scope  what happens to their review?
Eden (People Ops): default: review window is anchored to the current cycle. if scope changes materially, new manager can request a transfer recalibration (requires sign-off from both managers + People Ops).
Ari (IC): appeals timeline? some folks were unsure during the live Q&A.
Eden (People Ops): appeals window is 14 calendar days after the calibration email. managers file packets for direct reports; ICs should raise concerns with their manager first. we'll publish a tiny flowchart in the handbook update. :spiral_notepad:
Sofia (Recruiting): question for the doc where should recruiters record onboarding promises? Greenhouse Offer Notes ok?
Eden (People Ops): yes please record it in Greenhouse Offer Notes and attach the 1-paragraph onboarding promo plan or link to goals. that creates an audit trail.
Eden (People Ops): thanks all  i'll push a handbook snippet + templates by EOW and host a short manager office hour to walk through examples. drop any last follow-ups here before EOD. :raised_hands:
